Business Overview Hornbeck Offshore Services, Inc. is a premier offshore marine services company, combining world-class vessels, subsea robotics, emerging technologies, engineering expertise and offshore execution capabilities into a single integrated platform supporting major and independent oil and gas companies, oilfield service companies, renewable energy developers, the U.S. military, and offshore engineering, procurement, construction and installation contractors. We operate our core business through three segments: (1) Marine Transportation & Specialty, (2) Subsea Services, and (3) Well Intervention. We help customers solve complex offshore challenges and deliver comprehensive, integrated solutions to a diversified range of deepwater and ultra-deepwater operations around the world, primarily in the Gulf of America, Latin America, the North Sea, West Africa and Asia Pacific. With a diverse, technologically-advanced fleet of high-spec and ultra high-spec vessels and specialty assets, the combination of our marine transportation, subsea services and well intervention capabilities enables us to provide end-to-end integrated solutions throughout the entire life-of-field cycle for deepwater and ultra-deepwater offshore oilfield projects — spanning survey and exploration drilling support; subsea construction, installation and commissioning; inspection, repair and maintenance; production support; intervention and production enhancement; and decommissioning and abandonment activities. Additionally, our highly versatile fleet meets the growing offshore demands of several non-oilfield markets, such as offshore wind farm development, autonomous marine applications, defense and aerospace support. Marine Transportation & Specialty We provide transportation of equipment, materials and supplies to the offshore energy and defense industries through our Marine Transportation & Specialty segment. We also deliver a range of specialized services, including offshore accommodation and defense support. More recently, we have begun to provide vessels that are equipped with remote control/autonomous navigation technology to defense customers. 36 Our high spec and ultra high-spec OSVs are distinguished by industry-leading cargo and liquid mud capacities paired with advanced nautical technologies tailored for deepwater and ultra-deepwater operations. Complementing this, our accommodation vessel fleet provides a broad array of offshore housing and "walk-to-work" solutions — offering safe, dependable, and scalable options to serve the offshore wind and oilfield markets, along with other non-energy markets, such as HADR. Our specialty vessels further extend our capabilities providing customized marine solutions for the U.S. military, aerospace and telecommunications industries. Subsea Services Our service offerings to the offshore energy industry span a broad spectrum of deepwater and ultra-deepwater subsea services, encompassing subsea construction, trenching, IRM, survey, commissioning, field decommissioning and site clearance. Leveraging a versatile fleet of MPSVs, our Subsea Services segment deploys large subsea cranes with enhanced lifting capacities, seabed trenchers, cutting-edge robotics, and specialized tooling in support of complex offshore wind and oilfield projects. We own and operate one of the largest fleets of subsea trenchers in the world. Our extensive knowledge of seabed soil conditions, combined with advanced technology and best practices honed in global markets, allow us to deliver tailored, high-performance solutions that address some of the most complex subsea challenges in the world. Well Intervention Our Well Intervention segment provides rigless production enhancement and decommissioning services to the offshore energy industry with a focus on deepwater production maximization and well abandonment. Supported by our purpose-built well intervention vessels and subsea systems, our services provide a lower cost, higher efficiency with a reduced carbon footprint compared to rig-based intervention solutions. With work performed on over 2,000 subsea wells, our knowledge and experience in riser-based and riserless intervention offer customers a safe, reliable and economically advantageous solution to their deepwater intervention needs. We are the owner and operator of the largest fleet of intervention vessels in the world. We also provide access to designated vessels and equipment for emergency well containment response through the Helix Fast Response System, and own and operate a floating production unit providing oil and gas production processing services. Current Market Conditions and Outlook During the third quarter of 2026, offshore energy markets continued to demonstrate generally constructive fundamentals, supported by ongoing investment in deepwater oil and gas development, subsea infrastructure and production-related activity. Industry data indicate that offshore market conditions improved from late-2025 levels, although activity and pricing trends continued to vary by geography and asset class. Offshore project sanctioning remained active during 2026. Rystad Energy projected approximately $142 billion of global offshore upstream greenfield investment commitments for 2026, reflecting continued investment in offshore development activity. This level of project sanctioning, together with the existing base of producing offshore assets, supports prospective demand for marine transportation, subsea construction, robotics, well intervention and other life-of-field services. Conditions in the OSV market remained generally favorable, particularly for high-spec and ultra high-spec vessels, such as ours, although market conditions varied across vessel classes and geographic regions. Industry commentary during the third quarter cited firm utilization and limited supply growth as continuing supportive factors for the OSV market. The limited addition of new vessel capacity following an extended period of low newbuild investment continues to constrain available supply in certain higher-specification vessel categories and cabotage-protected markets. 37 The outlook for subsea and other life-of-field services remains generally constructive. Based upon market research published by Rystad Energy, global subsea spending is expected to increase from approximately $38 billion in 2026 to approximately $49 billion in 2030, while spending associated with offshore well intervention is also expected to grow as operators seek to maintain production and optimize recovery from an expanding and aging installed base of offshore wells and subsea infrastructure. The same research anticipates that a substantial number of offshore wells will become inactive between 2026 and 2030, potentially supporting increased demand for late-life services including intervention and decommissioning. The global offshore renewables market continues to develop, particularly in Europe and the Asia-Pacific region, supported by long-term renewable energy and energy security initiatives. Near-term market activity, particularly in Europe, has been affected by higher project costs, financing constraints, supply chain challenges and project delays. In the U.S., the offshore wind development market continues to face regulatory and policy uncertainty, which may result in project delays, cancellations or reduced development activity. These headwinds could lead to some softening in demand for offshore wind support services in the U.S. market. De spite these challenges, continued development of offshore wind projects is expected to provide opportunities for subsea construction, trenching, IRM and other subsea services. The Company believes these market conditions provide a constructive backdrop for its diversified portfolio of offshore services. Despite these favorable industry conditions, the pace of offshore activity remains subject to commodity prices, customer capital allocation, project timing, geopolitical developments, regional supply and demand conditions and other macroeconomic factors. As a result, market conditions and utilization and pricing trends may vary materially among the Company's business segments, operating regions and service offerings. Foreign Currency Exchange Rate Risk Because we operate in various regions around the world, we conduct a portion of our business in currencies other than the U.S. dollar. As such, our earnings are impacted by movements in foreign currency exchange rates when (i) transactions are denominated in currencies other than the functional currency of the relevant Hornbeck entity or (ii) the functional currency of our subsidiaries is not the U.S. dollar. In order to mitigate the effects of exchange rate risk in areas outside the U.S., we endeavor to pay a portion of our expenses in local currencies to partially offset revenues that are denominated in the same local currencies. In addition, a substantial portion of our contracts are denominated, and provide for collections from our customers, in U.S. dollars. Assets and liabilities of our subsidiaries that do not have the U.S. dollar as their functional currency are translated using the exchange rates in effect at the balance sheet date, and changes in the exchange rates can result in translation adjustments that are reflected in “Accumulated other comprehensive loss” in the stockholders’ equity section of the condensed consolidated balance sheets. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we recorded foreign currency translation losses of $13.5 million to accumulated other comprehensive loss. When currencies other than the functional currency are to be paid or received, the resulting transaction gain or loss associated with changes in the applicable foreign currency exchange rate is recognized in the condensed consolidated statements of operations as a component of “Other income (expense).” Foreign currency gains or losses from the remeasurement of monetary assets and liabilities as well as unsettled foreign currency transactions, including intercompany transactions that are not of a long-term investment nature, are also recognized as a component of “Other income (expense).” For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we recorded net foreign currency losses of $0.6 million primarily related to our international subsidiaries’ foreign currency positions. Interest Rate Risk In order to minimize the risk of changes to our cash flow due to changing interest rates, we generally borrow at fixed rates, but may borrow at variable rates from time to time. For fixed rate debt, changes in interest rates may not affect our interest expense, but could result in changes in the fair value of the debt instrument prior to maturity and we may be at risk upon refinancing maturing debt. For variable rate debt, changes in interest rates could affect our future interest expense and cash flows. Borrowings under the First Lien Revolving Credit Facility bear interest at variable rates based on Term SOFR or a base rate, plus an applicable margin. As of September 30, 2026, there were no borrowings outstanding under the First Lien Revolving Credit Facility. Commodity Price Risk We are exposed to market price risks related to oil and natural gas with respect to offshore oil and gas production related to our Droshky and Thunder Hawk properties. Prices are volatile and unpredictable and are dependent on many factors beyond our control.
